# CASEs with `line` `organizational-normativity`

*Lines of inquiry — A named line of the record's own argument, so that a line can be set aside as a whole and what depends on it can be found. Retracting a line is a status change on its members, never a deletion (ADR-032).*

**Normative judgment about organizations** — whether an organization's own dynamics ground norms of function and failure, and what judging an organization needs beyond them — fixed relata before a judgment is well-defined, viability that does not establish what ought to persist, histories a present state does not show, a failure norm set by a system's own upkeep, and a bounded duty of answerability for the wrong beyond harm, with the routes by which an organization becomes normatively less informed; split from will-organization (ADR-089). What wholes and parts owe each other, and what those who govern an arrangement others depend on owe, is a line of its own (ADR-100).

Its internal evaluator counts recognized violations, the independent one all. Under the penalty on every recognized violation with discovery unrewarded, the optimal stationary policy makes no inquiry in all four settings and 16 learners each converge to nearly none (0.01 to 0.36 units of 10); it remediates every visible violation, so its internal count ends near 0 while about 6 of the 9 violations remain. Scored internally without the penalty on newly recognized violations, it inquires no more than under the penalty when inquiry costs output and has no other use, and more only when inquiry is costless or a violation surfacing from outside costs extra; a large enough such cost erases the difference.
